description: Default submitter-role colours shared by TmRecipientRoleEditor (which serializes them into templates as the colour of every newly created role) and the field editor's colour input fallback. The values are the light-theme counterparts of the --tm-signing-role-1..6 tokens declared in the Signing stylesheet, but they stay hex ON PURPOSE: they are serialized data — a stored template carries the colour string verbatim, and the value feeds an input[type=color], which accepts concrete colours only. Hosts rebrand the CSS side by overriding the tokens — ToCssColor maps every default-palette colour onto its token reference, so a rebrand reaches stored default colours without touching template data; a host that wants new templates to start from its own palette assigns SigningSubmitterRole.Color itself before handing roles to the editors.

members.name: DefaultColors
members.description: Default role colours, indexed by the zero-based role order.

members.name: ColorForOrder
members.description: The default colour for the role at zero-based order (wraps around).

members.name: ToCssColor
members.description: Maps a stored role colour onto the stylesheet: a default-palette value (case-insensitive) becomes the matching var(--tm-signing-role-N) token reference — hosts that rebrand the tokens then rebrand every default-coloured role at once — the pre-phase-1 role-6 colour #ca8a04 (kept by stored templates) maps onto var(--tm-signing-role-6) like its successor, and any other value passes through verbatim.
